text:
maya: FYI customer acme-inc reported spike in p95/p99 during last billing window. They see 10-20x p99 for dedicated workloads, only when priority queue is active. stacktrace attached in ticket.

jonas: can you paste the top-level symptoms? is it auth 5xx or attach/queue latency?

maya: not auth — requests accepted, then long queue wait (~6-12s) then cold GPU attach + warmup. p95 jumps to 800ms->2.5s, p99 to 2s->10s. Happens during minute-aligned billing bursts.

priya: sounds like priority inversion in fairshare: low-priority tenants were preempted but their fairshare weights still causing attach fanout when queue flushes. any graphs?

maya: attaching perf screenshot snippet (copied):
```
time,attach_rate_qps,active_waiting,avg_warmup_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms
2026-03-17T16:00:00Z,120,340,520,2500,10000
2026-03-17T16:01:00Z,980,1500,600,2750,11000
```

jonas: can you share recent autoscale events from the pool for that minute?

maya: from logs: `pool=d-ed-45 events=[scale_request id=abc123 targets=12->60, provision_start=16:00:02, first_gpu_ready=16:00:08, handshake=16:00:12]` so ~10s to attach first usable GPU.

autoscale-bot: alert: dedicated-pool d-ed-45 cold-attach-duration > 8s (p99) — triggered at 4101234568

kevin: reasonable repro hypothesis: (1) min-pool too low for priority mix, (2) image-pull / kernel-cache thrash on surge, (3) attach-rate limiting and serialized init tasks cause head-of-line.

priya: agree. early mitigation options: bump min_pool for high-priority customers during billing window, enable pre-pull images on hosts for the pool, and temporarily route fallback traffic to hosted tier.

jonas: immediate small blast plan: 1) add `min_pool=10` for the affected pool, 2) enable fast-prewarm for acme-inc route (prefix caching), 3) set short-term priority-pin for their requests so they don't compete with lower-priority tenants. will this break fairness?

kevin: short-term is fine if documented to SRE. For fairness we can throttle background tenants by reducing their concurrency weight; that's reversible.

maya: internal ask from accts: they want a mitigation that doesn't change their code. routing fallback to hosted looks safest. cost implications expected.

priya: steps to implement (engineers):
- `infractl pools update d-ed-45 --min-pool 10 --prepull-images true`
- add route override: `routes set acme-inc --fallback-hosted true --priority-pin true --expiry 00:30:00`
- monitor `attach_duration_seconds{pool=\"d-ed-45\"}` and `waiting_queue_size{pool=\"d-ed-45\"}`

jonas: i'll run the min_pool change and watch metrics. pls stand by for logs.

autoscale-bot: runbook note created: "priority waiting-room / starvation" template applied to incident #INC-20260317-876

maya: quick repro notes for postmortem: 1) aligned billing windows create burst of short-lived jobs, 2) fairshare preemption leads to many concurrent attach attempts, 3) attach-controller serializes kernel init causing head-of-line and queue buildup.

kevin: longer-term fixes suggested: async attach pipeline (streaming kernel init), proactive scheduled prewarm for flagged billing windows, improvement to fairshare to avoid simultaneous flood after preemption (staggered backoff + randomized attach jitter).

priya: also consider per-customer min-pool and priority QoS config in console to let customers opt-in.

maya: notes for support response to customer: apologize, explain root cause (priority inversion + attach latency), outline immediate workaround (fallback to hosted or temporary priority pin + increased min_pool), offer credits if they prefer. cc @acme-inc contact.

jonas: live change applied: min_pool -> 10 at 16:03:40, observed waiting_queue drop 1500->120 in 40s, p99 reduced from ~11s -> ~1.4s.

maya: customer emailed: latency returning to baseline, wants writeup and follow-up call.

kevin: follow-up action items: A) implement attach jitter + randomized backoff B) support scheduled prewarm windows C) add autoscale metrics alert for `attach_rate > X and waiting_queue > Y` to auto-trigger prewarm or fallback routing.

priya: assigning tickets: INFRA-4523 (prewarm), RUNTIME-3390 (async attach), SUPPORT-1211 (customer follow-up).

maya: thanks team :thumbsup: I'll send the customer the mitigation summary and schedule call.

jonas: closing note: this was a nice example of "waiting-room" starvation where fairness policies cause a synchronized flood when preemption ends. keep an eye on similar patterns during invoice cycles.

maya: +1, added to incident retro.
